name: Pale Olive
lede: Pale olive is a light, yellowish green, the color name used for soft olive tones rather than the dark olive of the fruit.

sections.title: A modifier on olive
sections.body:
Pale olive is a descriptive name, a pale version of [[olive]], and the books use it as a plain description rather than a defined color. Paterson defines the related *mastic* as a pale olive brown, after the gum of the mastic tree [1]. The Pigment Compendium describes the copper mineral libethenite as occurring in pale olive green to dark green crystals, and notes it was described in 1823 [2].

Pale Olive Brown also appears as a paint name in a modern table that matches natural colors to pigments and paints [3]. So pale olive wording turns up in dictionaries, mineralogy and paint matching [1][2][3], though only the mineral entry uses the words pale olive green exactly.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of museum paintings, a color near this swatch is present in 20 works, 0.08 per cent of the archive [4]. The earliest is a 1506 work and the latest dates from 1941 [4]. As always, these are photographs of varnished paintings, so read them as screen colors [4].
